items.title: btc_dashboard tile status dot stays green while offline
items.detail: Spec 13 §2.5 / §8.7 and the Dart `_BtcDashboardTileContentState._load` (lib/screens/home_screen.dart:3561) set `_d` to the result of every `getDashboardData()`, dead ones included, and colour the dot `d != null && !d.isDead ? green α0.7 : grey`. Native HomeViewModel (feature/home/.../HomeViewModel.kt:109-118) builds `BtcUi.live` from `HomeDataSource.dashboard`, which is `MempoolService.lastDashboard`. MempoolServiceImpl only writes `lastDashboard` when `okCount > 0` ('a dead run never replaces a good dataset'). The result of `refreshDashboard()` (HomeDataSource.kt:313) is discarded. Once any run has succeeded, the tile dot therefore stays green even when every later poll is dead (device offline, IP blocked). This breaks the 'honest status UI' rule (§9.8). Repro: open Home online, switch on airplane mode, wait 60 s. Flutter shows a grey dot; native stays green. Fix: keep the last result of the tile's own poll (dead included) in HomeViewModel and use it for `live`. Use `lastDashboard` only for the initial value.

items.title: BTC tile shows "0" instead of "––" when the block height is unknown
items.detail: Dart (home_screen.dart:3655) renders `d != null && d.blockHeight > 0 ? _fmtInt(d.blockHeight) : '––'`. Native HomeViewModel.kt:114 renders `d?.let { BtcFormat.fmtInt(it.blockHeight) } ?: DASH`, so a dataset with `blockHeight == 0` shows `0`. That happens when the first ever successful run had a failed height source and no `mempool_last_height` is stored yet. Use `BtcFormat.intOrDash(d.blockHeight.toLong())`.

items.title: BTC tile re-fetches on every return to Home, not on a 60 s cadence
items.detail: Spec 13 §2.5 / §5.7: the tile loads once on creation and then every 60 s, and the request rate should stay at most about 2 dashboard runs per minute. Native HomeViewModel.onStart() (HomeViewModel.kt:140-148) starts a new loop with an immediate `refreshDashboard()` each time Home reaches STARTED. Opening the Bitcoin dashboard (which loads on open) and going back fires another 6 requests at once, and repeated back-and-forth navigation multiplies the mempool.space load (risk of 429 / 'blocked'). Skip the immediate refresh when the last tile load is newer than 60 s, as BitcoinDashboardViewModel.autoRefreshWhileVisible already does.

items.title: Identity switch via nsec import or Amber/NIP-46 connect keeps the old identity's platform and humanity proofs
items.detail: Spec 06 §14 R20 (and §9 'On identity switch, the old identity's proofs are wiped') says every native path that switches identity (import nsec, connect a different signer, restore a backup) must call clearForIdentitySwitch() or clear the proofs, as the badge-sync flow does. Today only the backup restore and badge-sync settle paths do it (DefaultRestoreEngine:310/434, DefaultBadgeSync.settleLocked:564 -> HumanityProofRepository.clearForIdentitySwitch). ProfileEditViewModel.importNsec() (feature/profile/.../edit/ProfileEditViewModel.kt:396-420), connectAmber() (:517-536) and onBunkerFinished() (:545-559) switch the npub and only show a 'profileIdentityChanged' warning snackbar (warnIfIdentityChanged). platform_proofs and humanity_* stay in place. ReputationPublishStartupTask fires on SigningService.signerReady, and DefaultReputationPublisher always embeds getProofsForPublishing() and getProofForPublishing(). So the next publish puts kind-21003 signatures made by the old key, plus the old key's humanity_proof, into the new key's kind-30078 event. Repro: have a local key with a Telegram proof and humanity verified, then import a different nsec in the profile. The profile tiles still show '1 Plattform aktiv' and 'Lightning-Beweis aktiv', and the reputation event of the new npub carries platform_proofs.telegram. Fix: when the npub changes (previous non-empty and different), call HumanityProofRepository.clearForIdentitySwitch(). Better: do it centrally with a SigningService identity-changed hook in :data:identity, collected by a :data:proofs startup task, so onboarding and settings paths are covered too. Flutter has no clear here, but spec R20 requires it for the native app.

items.title: Create result snackbar is lost if the user leaves the platform proof screen while the signer is open
items.detail: Spec 06 §2.1 generateProof: on success, green ppLinkSaved snackbar (3 s) on the root messenger, then pop. On failure, red 10 s dismissable snackbar. PlatformProofsViewModel.create() runs sign, store and republish in @ApplicationScope (good, the proof is still saved). The result is only reported through _events from viewModelScope (PlatformProofsViewModel.kt:178-187) and collected by the route's LaunchedEffect. If the user backs out while Amber or a NIP-46 bunker is pending, the nav entry's ViewModel is cleared. The work finishes, but neither the 'Verknüpfung gespeichert!' snackbar nor the failure message (for example 'Permission denied for sign_event kind:21003') is ever shown. Flutter's future kept running and showed the snackbar on the root messenger. Fix: when the VM is gone, post the outcome to the app-level snackbar host from the appScope job (showLinkSavedOnAppHost already exists for the success case).

items.title: Verify-string screen still says the platform-proof signature was checked (S-9 fix only half done)
items.detail: Spec 04 §9 S-9 / R-16: the 21rep verify-string sig is only checked for format (bech32 npub plus 128 hex chars), never cryptographically. The native port should not claim cryptographic verification unless the proof is in the author's signed kind 30078 (proofInEvent). The scanner result screen does this correctly: QR `pp` rows use native_qrLinkedUnconfirmed in amber. ReputationVerifyScreen does not. For VerifyLevel.SIGNATURE_ONLY it shows the header `rvSignatureOnly` ("NUR SIGNATUR GEPRÜFT"). The message strings in feature/reputation/src/main/res/values*/strings.xml still claim a valid signature: native_rvMsgNoReputation "Signatur gültig ✓ — Aber keine Reputation auf Relays gefunden." and native_rvMsgSignatureOnlyNoBindings "Signatur gültig, aber keine gebundenen Badges.". Repro: enter `21rep::<valid npub>::telegram::x::sig=<any 128 hex>` for an npub that has no reputation event. The result reads "Signatur gültig ✓" although nothing was verified. Fix: reword these two messages (de/en/es) and the SIGNATURE_ONLY header to something like "Format gültig / verknüpft (unbestätigt)". Files: feature/reputation/.../verify/ReputationVerifyScreen.kt (ResultHeader), common/Messages.kt, res/values*/strings.xml.

items.title: Export share fallback reports success when the share chooser could not be started
items.detail: Spec 08 §2.4 steps 11–13, §9 #13 and §14 risk 11 say export must never return true unless a file was saved or a share target was chosen, because the reset flow wipes keys and badges when export returns true. In core/ui/.../share/ShareHelper.kt `startChooserForResult`, when `launch(context, chooser)` fails (it catches ActivityNotFoundException and returns false), the result is `ShareResult.Unavailable`. `ShareResult.isNotDismissed` (ShareResult.kt:36) counts Unavailable as shared. BackupCoordinator.runExport (feature/backup BackupCoordinator.kt, `shareUntilDetached(...).isNotDismissed`) then returns true, so HomeViewModel.onResetCreateBackup shows 'Backup erstellt. Jetzt zurücksetzen?' even though no file was written or shared. In Flutter, a share that fails to start throws a PlatformException, which shows the red `backupError` snackbar and returns false. Repro: SAF CreateDocument is cancelled or unavailable, and startActivity(chooser) throws. Fix: return a distinct failure result (or Dismissed) when the chooser launch fails, and keep Unavailable only for the case where the chooser started but its outcome cannot be observed. Optionally show `backupError` for the launch failure.

items.title: Start flow aborts with an error snackbar when session creation fails; Flutter still records attendance and opens the QR screen
items.detail: Spec 05 §2.2.3 and risk 18: in Dart, RollingQRService.getOrCreateSession may return null. The flow then still awaits CoAttendanceService.recordOrganizerAttendance(blockHeight: session?.blockHeight ?? 0), calls _checkSession() and pushes RollingQRScreen. Native: DefaultOrganizerSessionService.startMeetupSession (data/issuance/.../internal/DefaultOrganizerSessionService.kt) calls rollingQr.getOrCreateSession, which throws SessionStartException instead of returning null. AdminPanelViewModel.runStartFlow (feature/admin/.../AdminPanelViewModel.kt) catches the exception and shows only the red wotErrorShort snackbar. As a result, the organizer marker badge and the kind-30079 organizer publish are skipped, and no navigation happens. Risk 18 explicitly allows surfacing an error instead, so this may be intended. If so, document it as a deliberate deviation. Otherwise, call recordOrganizerAttendance before rethrowing. Repro: start a meetup while signing fails (e.g. the external signer rejects). Flutter navigates to the QR screen; native shows 'Fehler: …' and stays on the panel.

items.title: VerifyPerson path tap does not fall back to njump.me when the nostr: launch throws SecurityException
items.detail: Spec 05 §2.3 item 7 and the §2.1 open-in-Nostr rule: if launching nostr:<npub> returns false or throws, Dart opens https://njump.me/<npub> instead. In feature/reputation/.../common/ReputationUi.kt, openNostr() falls back only on ActivityNotFoundException. A SecurityException is only logged, so tapping a path node does nothing. The trust-network screen's own openInNostr (feature/network/MyNetworkScreen.kt) handles both exceptions correctly. Fix: on SecurityException, also call SafeUrlLauncher.open(context, NpubFormat.profileUrl(npub)).

items.title: Shared PNGs in cacheDir/share are never cleaned up (world-map images pile up)
items.detail: Spec 03 §11 (Share row) says to write share files to cacheDir/shared and to "Clean up old files". §9.7 adds that the world-map image reveals the user's location history. ShareHelper.writePng (core/ui/src/main/kotlin/space/einundzwanzig/meetup/core/ui/share/ShareHelper.kt) writes to cacheDir/share/ and nothing ever deletes these files. A grep for shareDir/SHARE_DIR finds no cleanup anywhere. BadgeWorldMapScreen shares `badge_worldmap_<millis>.png` (feature/wallet/.../map/BadgeWorldMapScreen.kt, WorldMap.fileName), so every map share leaves a new file with the user's location history in the app cache until the OS evicts it. einundzwanzig_badge.png is overwritten each time, so only the map files accumulate. Repro: share the world map 3 times, then `run-as space.einundzwanzig.meetup ls cache/share`; there are 3 badge_worldmap_*.png files. Fix: delete old files in shareDir before writing (for example files older than 1 h, or all files with the same prefix), or clean up on app start.

items.title: Cleartext exception for 127.0.0.1/localhost kept although the native PlebRap player uses no loopback proxy
items.detail: Spec 11 §9 item 11 says Flutter allowed cleartext to 127.0.0.1/localhost only for the just_audio loopback cache proxy, and that a native Media3 implementation 'should NOT need any cleartext exception — drop it if unused'. The native player (data/community plebrap: ExoPlaybackBackend + Media3AudioCache/SimpleCache) streams over https and reads from the Media3 cache. It opens no local HTTP server: a grep for 127.0.0.1/localhost/ServerSocket in non-test Kotlin finds nothing PlebRap-related. Even so, app/src/main/res/xml/network_security_config.xml still has the 'Ausnahme 3' domain-config (cleartextTrafficPermitted=true for 127.0.0.1 and localhost), and its comment still describes the just_audio proxy. core/network CleartextPolicy.isCleartextPermitted mirrors this by allowing 127.0.0.1/localhost. Fix: remove the loopback domain-config and the matching CleartextPolicy branch, unless another domain can be shown to need it (check spec 13 mempool custom server first; only .onion/.local are justified there). Update the CleartextPolicy tests to match.

items.title: Location permission is never requested: LocationPermissionBridge has no Activity collector
items.detail:
Spec 09 §8.5 / §2.2 init step 1 / §11: getCurrentLocation() must prompt for ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION + ACCESS_COARSE_LOCATION when the permission is not granted. In the native code the prompt goes through data/meetups/.../location/LocationPermissionBridge.kt. Its KDoc says MainActivity has to collect `pendingRequest` and launch `RequestMultiplePermissions`, but nothing in :app (MainActivity.kt only wires `signerLauncher` and `externalSignerBridge`) or in any feature module collects it. A repo-wide grep finds no location RequestPermission(s) launcher at all; the only runtime permission request is CAMERA in :core:camera. LocationPermissionBridgeImpl.request() returns DENIED immediately when `state.subscriptionCount == 0`.
Result: on a fresh install, or whenever the permission is not already granted (for example carried over from the Flutter app), Nearby "Hier & jetzt" always shows the location-denied hint and "Standort erneut versuchen" can never fix it. LocationPicker "Zu meinem Standort" always shows "Standort nicht verfügbar". Every badge-domain consumer of MeetupLocationService.getCurrentLocation/resolveLocation (organizer session radius, participant 5/50 km presence checks, event badges) gets DENIED and never shows the system dialog.
Fix: in MainActivity, register `registerForActivityResult(RequestMultiplePermissions())`. Collect `bridge.pendingRequest` while STARTED; when `onLaunched(id)` is true, launch with both permissions. In the callback call `bridge.onResult(granted = any granted, permanentlyDenied = !granted && !shouldShowRequestPermissionRationale(FINE) && !shouldShowRequestPermissionRationale(COARSE))`. The bridge must be exposed for injection: it is bound as `LocationPermissionBridge` in MeetupsModule. Repro: install fresh → bottom bar "In der Nähe" → no system dialog, hint row shown immediately.

items.title: Signer disconnect reloads only the identity, not the full profile (Dart calls _loadData)
items.detail: Spec 07 §2.2.4 says that after a disconnect is confirmed, a full `loadData()` runs before the `profileDisconnectDone` snackbar (profile_edit.dart:535). That call resets the nickname field, the selected home and favourites, and `isEditing = !user.isAdminVerified`. ProfileEditViewModel.disconnect() only calls reloadIdentity() (hasLocalKey/mode/canSign/npub), so unsaved form input stays. A verified organizer who pressed 'BEARBEITEN (Status verlieren)' also stays in edit mode, where Dart drops back to read-only. The native behaviour is arguably better, but it is not parity. Decide whether to keep it and document it, or call loadData() here. File: feature/profile/.../edit/ProfileEditViewModel.kt disconnect().

items.title: Profile screen adds a gallery avatar picker and shows the local picture, which Flutter's profile screen does not
items.detail: Dart ProfileEditScreen has no avatar in the edit form. The read-only view shows only `NostrAvatar(radius 44, green)` from the kind-0 picture (spec 07 §2.2.1 item 1). Natively, EditForm renders an editable ProfileAvatar: tapping it opens PickVisualMedia → LocalPictureImporter → `local_profile_picture`. Both views also show `local_profile_picture` before the Nostr picture. In Dart the local picture and its picker exist only on the Home header, and there the picker opens only when there is no Nostr picture (spec 12 F14). Native profile always allows picking. This is extra functionality outside spec 07; confirm it is intended. File: feature/profile/.../edit/ProfileEditScreen.kt ProfileAvatar / EditForm.

items.title: Widget refresh worker overwrites the news row when the feed returns no article
items.detail: app/src/main/kotlin/space/einundzwanzig/meetup/widget/WidgetRefresh.kt:87-88 calls `widgetStore.publishLatestNews(latest?.id.orEmpty(), latest?.title ?: "News")` even when `news.fetchArticles(limit = 1)` returns an empty list. DefaultNewsService.fetchArticles returns [] on network or feed failure (Dart parity). Dart `WidgetService.refreshNews` (lib/services/widget_service.dart:120-121) does `if (articles.isEmpty) return;`. Spec 10 §2.10 says "if any: …", and spec 14 §3.2 says the worker "writes like refreshNews". Native behaviour: an offline tap on ⟳ (or a feed hiccup) sets the widget newsTitle to "News", sets newsIsNew=false and writes widget_latest_news_id/widget_latest_news_title to ""/"News". The last good headline and the NEU marker are lost, and a later markNewsSeen() has no id to record. Home's own path (HomeDataSource.publishLatestNews, `firstOrNull() ?: return`) is correct. Fix: return early in refreshWidget when there is no article.

items.title: KeyValueStore/SecureStore are not gated by the migration, and pending Flutter secrets are never reported as Unreadable
items.detail: Spec 14 §4.7 and R3 require two things. First, KeyValueStore and SecureStore must await a MigrationGate (interface in :core:data) before their first read or write. Second, while a Flutter secret is still pending, SecureStore.readChecked(key) must return Unreadable so that no domain generates a replacement key (Dart resetOnError:false). Neither is implemented. core/data has no gate and no pending mapping (grep finds no 'gate'/'pending' in core/data/src/main). FlutterMigration.pendingLegacySecrets() has no caller outside :data:migration, which can be checked by grepping feature/, data/identity and data/badges. data/migration/README.md marks this itself as 'RELEASE BLOCKER ... gating is not wired yet'. The only protection is that MainActivity does not compose before the gate completes, and that only holds for the current attempt. Repro: an E1 device whose ESP master alias is gone (ESP_MASTER_KEY_MISSING), or any IMPORTED_WITH_ERRORS outcome where nostr_nsec_key or badge_encryption_key failed. The gate completes and nostr_nsec_key reads Absent. SplashRouting sends the user to onboarding and they create a new identity, or the badge repo creates a new badge key. On a later retryNow() the Flutter value is only written to legacy_recovered/<key>, and no UI offers it (see the identity-recovery issue). Fix as the README describes: add a MigrationGate and LegacySecretStatus interface in :core:data, have both stores await the gate, map pending keys to SecureRead.Unreadable(PENDING_MIGRATION), and give the migration @Ungated store bindings.

items.title: No UI for parked Flutter identities (legacy_esp/legacy_backup/legacy_recovered): no restore/export notice
items.detail: Spec 14 §4.8 (ESP row, R5): an ESP identity that does not match an npub still referenced in the prefs goes to legacy_esp/<key>, 'and a one-time notice in the identity area offering restore/export'. :data:identity implements the API (IdentityRecovery.candidates/adopt/exportNsec/discard in data/identity/.../keys/IdentityRecovery.kt). No feature module uses it: grepping IdentityRecovery across feature/ and app/ finds nothing. Users in the F1 case (key lost by Flutter 1.7.x) and every retry conflict (legacy_recovered/) therefore cannot get their old identity back, even though the migration recovered it. Needed: a one-time notice in the identity/profile area with adopt (confirmation, then LocalKeyVault.clearAll + useLocalMode) and export behind DeviceAuthenticator, SecureDialog and SecretClipboard, plus discard.

items.title: Settings → Diagnose lacks 'Alte Daten erneut übernehmen' (retryNow) and the give-up action (abandonPendingSecrets)
items.detail: Spec 14 §4.7: after IMPORTED_WITH_ERRORS, automatic retries stop after 10 attempts, and later attempts are 'only from Settings → Diagnose ("Alte Daten erneut übernehmen", native_ string)'. FlutterMigration.retryNow() and abandonPendingSecrets() (the confirmed give-up for ESP_MASTER_KEY_MISSING or TOO_MANY_ATTEMPTS, documented in the README) have no caller in any feature module (grep for retryNow/abandonPendingSecrets outside data/migration finds nothing; feature/settings has no migration strings). Safe mode (R6) can only be left via retryNow(), so a device that hits it never imports its encrypted secrets again. Add a diagnostics entry that shows currentReport() state, failed key names and recovered names, a retry button, and a confirmed abandon action.

items.title: Release CI/signing pipeline from §5.2.1/§5.2.7 not implemented (cert pin, 16 KB check, mapping upload, exported allow-list, release naming)
items.detail: The only native workflow is .github/workflows/native_android_prerelease.yml. It builds only the preview variant (different applicationId, test key). No job builds and signs the release APK with the KEYSTORE_BASE64/KEYSTORE_* secrets. Also missing: the RELEASE_CERT_SHA256 apksigner pin check (F3/R1), the `zipalign -c -P 16` check (§5.2.6), mapping.txt upload (§5.2.4), the einundzwanzig-meetup-v${versionName}-${date}.apk naming (Obtainium continuity, §5.3), and the merged-manifest exported allow-list check (§6). In app/build.gradle.kts the release signing reads env vars RELEASE_STORE_FILE/RELEASE_STORE_PASSWORD/RELEASE_KEY_ALIAS/RELEASE_KEY_PASSWORD instead of the spec's E21_KEYSTORE_FILE/E21_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD/E21_KEY_ALIAS/E21_KEY_PASSWORD; a release job must use those names. The no-debug-fallback signing itself is correct.

items.title: FlutterMigration.cleanupIfEligible() is never called, so Flutter files, orphaned ESP secrets and Keystore aliases are never removed
items.detail: Spec 14 §4.7 Cleanup and the README wiring ('From the release AFTER the first native one, once per start: flutterMigration.cleanupIfEligible()'). EinundzwanzigApp.onCreate only calls ensureMigrated(), and there is no AppStartupTask that calls cleanupIfEligible. The method guards itself (NotYet RELEASE/STARTS/...), so it is safe to wire now. Without it, FlutterSecureStorage.xml (ESP entries, _BACKUP ciphertexts), FlutterSecureKeyStorage.xml, the snapshot copy in noBackupFilesDir and the three legacy aliases stay on the device forever. An incomplete RESET delete is also never finished.

items.title: IdentityRecovery ignores overflow recovery slots '<name>#n'
items.detail: When the plain recovery name already holds a different value, DefaultFlutterMigration.writeRecovery writes to overflow slots legacy_*/<key>#2..#16. DefaultIdentityRecovery (line ~128) filters with `k.substringAfter('/') in IdentityKeys.IDENTITY_SECRET_NAMES`, so 'nostr_nsec_key#2' never matches and the value is kept but never offered. EncryptedBadgeRepository.isIdentitySecret has the same gap and treats a '#n' identity copy as a badge-key candidate (harmless, but inconsistent). The README lists this as an open follow-up: strip substringBefore('#').

items.title: Widget provider and refresh worker continue after a 10 s / 20 s gate timeout instead of awaiting the migration
items.detail: Spec 14 §3.2/§4.7: Glance provideGlance and every Worker await the gate. MeetupWidget.provideGlance uses withTimeoutOrNull(10.seconds){gate.await()}, and WidgetRefreshWorker uses 20 s, then read and write anyway. The worker calls BitcoinWidgetBridge, which reads mempool_host/fiat_currency from KeyValueStore, and NewsService. On a slow Keystore/Tink migration, which is exactly the R6 scenario, they read empty native stores (default host/currency), and the widget renders without the migrated values. Without store-level gating this is the only protection, so the timeouts should go or the stores must be gated.

items.title: Launcher label changes from '21Meetup' to 'Einundzwanzig' on update
items.detail: Spec 14 §1.6/R19 recommends keeping '21Meetup' for continuity. app/src/main/res/values/app_name.xml has app_name = 'Einundzwanzig' (the Flutter manifest used android:label="21Meetup"). The widget receiver label is already '21Meetup' (native_widget_label), so the launcher and the widget picker now show different names. This needs a product decision; the default should be '21Meetup'.

items.title: Widget picker preview shows Glance's loading layout instead of a preview

On API 31+, previewLayout takes precedence over previewImage, so the launcher's widget picker shows an empty 'loading' box where Flutter showed the app icon (previewImage @mipmap/ic_launcher). Spec §1.3/§3.2 asks for a real previewLayout: add a static RemoteViews layout with the widget design, or drop previewLayout so previewImage is used.

items.title: Lightning wallet chooser title not localized

ValueForValueScreen calls LightningInvoiceLauncher.openWithChooser(context, event.invoice) without a chooserTitle, so the hard-coded German DEFAULT_CHOOSER_TITLE 'Lightning-Wallet wählen' appears in en/es as well. items.title: Extra exported component (PlebrapPlaybackService) beyond the §6 exported allow-list
items.detail: Spec 14 §6 (Audit N4): only .MainActivity is exported, plus library components that require it, and CI should check this. data/community's manifest declares PlebrapPlaybackService exported="true" (MediaSessionService, with a ConnectionGate in onConnect), and the app adds POST_NOTIFICATIONS/FOREGROUND_SERVICE_MEDIA_PLAYBACK. The spec allows these permissions only 'if the PlebRap player gets a media notification'. Acceptable if intended, but it should be recorded as an explicit allow-list entry and covered by the merged-manifest CI check, which does not exist (see the CI issue).

items.title: No instrumented (androidTest) migration / release-variant tests
items.detail: Spec 14 §4.11 asks for instrumented tests on API 26/29/34/36 that reproduce real FSS RSA aliases (exact KeyGenParameterSpec), a wrapped AES-128 key and an ESP file written through the vendored ESP class, then run the reader. §5.2.4 asks for release-variant checks on the minified migrationTest build: Schnorr, NIP-44, NIP-49, NavKey restore after process death, osmdroid, ML Kit, the ESP path. No androidTest source set exists in the project. The JVM/Robolectric suites (about 100 tests in data/migration) use a fake LegacyKeystore and cannot cover AndroidKeyStore 'AndroidKeyStoreBCWorkaround' unwrap or real Tink keyset parsing against a Keystore master key.

items.title: Signer and key service error messages are never localized (spec 01 §8.10)
items.detail: Spec 01 §8.10 asks for string resources (errSignCancelledAmber, errAmberMissing, errWrongAccount, errNoPrivateKey, errSignerNoEvent/KindChanged/ContentChanged/BadSig, errBunkerNoAnswer, errBunkerRejected, errModeAmberNoKey/Nip07NoKey/BunkerNoKey, errNoBunkerSession, errNip07WebOnly, and every Nip46Exception, Nip49Exception and LocalEasyAuthException text), German by default plus en and es. :data:identity defines the typed `SigningError` (SigningExceptions.kt) so features could show localized text, but no module reads `SigningError` (grep finds no consumer outside data/identity), and none of these resources exists in core/l10n or any feature `res/values*`. As a result the hard-coded German service texts are shown raw in every locale: in the IdentitySetup error box (`UiText.Raw(messageOf(e))` for register/import/resume: "Bitte einen Namen wählen.", "Ungültiges Format. Der Key muss mit \"nsec1\" beginnen.", "Falsches Passwort — oder der Schlüssel ist beschädigt."), in the bunker sheet error (Nip46ConnectResult.Error / Nip46Exception text, e.g. "In der Bunker-Adresse fehlt ein Relay …"), in the profile nsec import error (`UiText.Raw(e.message)`), and in errorAmber(detail). To reproduce: set the app language to English, open IdentitySetup → Schon Nostr → Anderer Weg, type `abc` and tap Import. The German FormatException text appears. items.title: ncryptsec import does not catch scrypt OutOfMemoryError (logN 16, 64 MiB)
items.detail: Spec 01 §7.2 and risk 11 say BouncyCastle scrypt allocates 64 MiB on the Java heap, so the port must catch OutOfMemoryError and show a user-visible error. DefaultLocalEasyAuth.scrypt{} does this, but DefaultNostrKeyService.importNcryptsec (data/identity/.../internal/DefaultNostrKeyService.kt) runs `withContext(cpu) { Nip49.decrypt(...) }` with no OOM handling. IdentitySetupViewModel.importKey only catches Exception, so an OOM while importing an `ncryptsec1…` key on a low-RAM device crashes the app instead of showing an error. Fix: wrap the call like LocalEasyAuth.scrypt and map the error to a LocalEasyAuthException/KeyFormatException message.

items.title: Profile ncryptsec export does not catch scrypt OutOfMemoryError
items.detail: ProfileEditViewModel.encryptWithPassword runs `withContext(encodeDispatcher) { ncryptsecEncoder(privHex, password) }` (Nip49.encrypt, logN 16, 64 MiB scrypt) and catches only Nip49Exception and Exception. An OutOfMemoryError is an Error, not an Exception, so it propagates and crashes the app. Spec 01 §7.2 and risk 11 require it to become a user-visible error through _showError. Reproduce on a low-heap device: Profile → VERSCHLÜSSELT EXPORTIEREN → Andere Passwort / no vault wrap → enter password. Fix: catch OutOfMemoryError there (or route the call through a shared scrypt helper in :data:identity) and call showError(errorGeneric).

items.title: "Mit Passkey sichern" step is never offered: PASSKEY_RP_ASSOCIATED defaults to false and no build sets it
items.detail: Spec 01 §2.3.4 and §2.3.6 say that after "Loslegen" the user goes to the passkey step when PasskeyPrfService.isSupported() is true. AndroidPasskeyPrfService.isSupported() returns false unless BuildConfig.PASSKEY_RP_ASSOCIATED is true. That flag comes only from the Gradle property `passkeyRpAssociated` (data/identity/build.gradle.kts), and no CI workflow or tools script sets it, so every native build skips the passkey step. Flutter showed the step, and the step then failed with idSetupPasskeyUnavailable. Spec 14 F9 documents this as an intentional deviation until assetlinks.json is deployed. Unlocking an existing (migrated) passkey wrap is not gated and still works. Flagging it so that the release pipeline gets `-PpasskeyRpAssociated=true` once https://einundzwanzig.space/.well-known/assetlinks.json is live. Otherwise passkey creation stays missing even after the domain is fixed.

items.title: App reset keeps the diagnostic 'verbose' flag (and log file) that Flutter's prefs.clear() removed
items.detail: Spec 12 §2.5.12 / §4: in Flutter, `SharedPreferences.clear()` removes `diagnostic_verbose` (and `diagnostic_log`), so after a reset and restart verbose logging is OFF. Natively, the log buffer and verbose flag live in `FileLogStore` (filesDir/diagnostic_log.jsonl, filesDir/diagnostic_verbose, per 00-contradictions #3), and `ResetAppUseCase.reset()` (feature/home/.../reset/ResetAppUseCase.kt) never touches them: no `log.setVerbose(false)` and no store reset. Repro: Settings > Diagnose-Log > enable verbose; App zurücksetzen; restart. Verbose logging is still on (DEBUG entries keep being recorded, 'Ausfuehrliches Log ist AKTIV.' appears in the APP-START block). Fix: call `log.setVerbose(false)` as an optional step in ResetAppUseCase. Optionally also clear the log, although Dart effectively rewrote the in-memory buffer on the next write.
